text:
maria: Quick heads-up 0min: PR #5427 (optimize toolkit examples) is marked ready but CI link-check flagged two dead links and reviewers noted the snippets are too dense. Need a small docs sprint to split examples and add streaming snippets.

sam: I can rework the streaming snippets. Preference: show SSE server-side sample as the primary example and add a compact WebSocket appendix. Also include a one-line resume token example.

maria: Yup, SSE primary. Keep the snippet tiny for copy-paste. Add a short note: avoid printing raw chunks in production.

ben: I'll split the batching example into two focused snippets: "latency-preferred" (web / interactive) and "throughput-optimized" (bulk inference). Will provide YAML for both.

jess: Also: quant profile names changed in runtime v1.3. Docs currently reference `q4_0` and `q8_0`. Runtime now exposes `q4f`, `q8f`, and `q4f_v2`. We need a one-paragraph migration note mapping old->new and a recommended use-case line. Keep it short.

kai: I'll backport the mapping paragraph to the /v1 docs after we finalize wording. I have the runtime release note link ready.

docs-bot: link-check: /optimize/quant -> 404, /sdk/python/streaming -> 404 :warning:

sam: Proposed minimal SSE (Python) for docs:
```python
# minimal SSE streaming (Redwood SDK v2)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
with client.text.stream(model="redwood/fast-1", mode="sse") as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        # in production, process tokens instead of printing raw chunks
        emit_token(chunk.text)
```
Add one-liner resume example: `resume = StreamResumeToken.from_last(chunk)` and show how to pass `resume_token=resume` on reopen.

ben: YAML for configs: latency-preferred first (small batches, kv prefetch):
```yaml
serving_config:
  batching:
    mode: latency-preferred
    max_batch_size: 8
    max_wait_ms: 20
  caching:
    kv_prefetch: true
    kv_prefetch_window: 32
```
Throughput example (microbatch, prefix cache):
```yaml
serving_config:
  batching:
    mode: microbatch
    max_batch_size: 128
    max_wait_ms: 150
  caching:
    prefix_cache: true
    prefix_cache_ttl_sec: 600
```
I'll keep examples as tiny blocks with comments.

jess: For the quant paragraph I suggest: "Note: runtime v1.3 renamed `q4_0`->`q4f` and `q8_0`->`q8f`. A newer variant `q4f_v2` offers improved throughput with modest quality regressions in edge cases. For short-sequence web workloads prefer `q4f`; for max throughput evaluate `q4f_v2` on your eval set." Link to runtime notes.

maria: Perfect. Make the paragraph 2-3 sentences max and include a tiny migration snippet: `old: q4_0 -> new: q4f`.

docs-bot: Reminder: docs linter rule: code blocks must wrap at 80 chars and files must pass link-check on push.

sam: I'll open a PR with the SSE + WebSocket appendix + link fixes. Ben, ping when your YAMLs are ready so I can update the examples page and remove the large monolith.

ben: Will push two small commits in my branch: `split-batching-snippets` and `yaml-examples-tidy`.

kai: Once the main PR merges, I'll backport quant mapping to /v1/docs and attach the runtime release URL.

maria: Action items: 
- sam: submit streaming snippet + WebSocket appendix + fix broken links
- ben: split batching examples, add the two YAML configs and a 1-line kv_prefetch note
- jess: add quant mapping paragraph + runtime link
- kai: backport mapping to v1/doc on merge
- maria: review & merge within 48h if CI green

sam: A small wording ask: any preferred phrasing for the resume token example?

ben: Keep it short: `# resume from last successful chunk with StreamResumeToken` then the one-liner.

jess: Pushed a draft for the mapping paragraph: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5433 (will update with runtime link)

maria: Thanks all. Ping here when PRs are opened and I'll prioritize reviews. :thumbsup:
